campaignLedger.title: $100 registration relief and a $50 weekly toll cap
campaignLedger.summary: The 2026–27 Budget included a 12-month transport affordability package: $100 off private vehicle registration, a lower $50 weekly toll cap and Opal fares held at 2025 prices.
campaignLedger.costing: $561.4 million package stated in the Budget material.
campaignLedger.geography: Statewide registration and public transport measures; toll relief is concentrated among eligible Sydney motorway users.
campaignLedger.verification: Funded Budget measure. Check commencement, eligibility, take-up and whether any element is extended beyond the stated 12 months.

campaignLedger.title: Health, schools and Western Sydney infrastructure package
campaignLedger.summary: Budget highlights list $10.3 billion for increased health services, including higher wages, 9,000 additional workers and 2,900 extra surgeries a year; $9.2 billion for more than 260 new or upgraded schools; and $3.5 billion extra for Western Sydney transport and roads.
campaignLedger.costing: Headline multi-year Budget allocations; do not add them without checking time periods and overlaps.
campaignLedger.geography: Statewide services with explicit Western Sydney and regional project components.
campaignLedger.verification: Build a project-level ledger: new versus previously announced money, delivery year, output target and electorate footprint.

campaignLedger.title: Payroll tax threshold and rate changes
campaignLedger.summary: Opposition Leader Kellie Sloane proposed lifting the payroll tax threshold from $1.2 million to $1.5 million and cutting the rate from 5.45% to 4.75% for businesses with payrolls below $10 million.
campaignLedger.costing: The ABC report said a total state-budget cost was not provided in the speech; the opposition said an eligible business could save up to $75,850.
campaignLedger.geography: Statewide, with effects varying by employer payroll and location.
campaignLedger.verification: Seek Treasury-style aggregate costings, interaction with existing thresholds, number of eligible firms and implementation date.

campaignLedger.title: South-west Metro planning, contribution freeze and Long Bay housing
campaignLedger.summary: The opposition outlined a new city deal with Canberra and a south-west Sydney Metro plan, repeated a proposal to freeze developer contributions on new houses until mid-2029, and proposed closing Long Bay Correctional Complex to pursue 12,000 homes while relocating prisoners to regional NSW.
campaignLedger.costing: Funding and delivery detail remained incomplete in the cited report.
campaignLedger.geography: South-west Sydney, Long Bay and regional correctional locations; statewide housing-market implications.
campaignLedger.verification: Separate planning target from delivered dwellings; test land, remediation, transport, prison-capacity and Commonwealth dependencies.

campaignLedger.title: Renewable Energy Zone redesign
campaignLedger.summary: The opposition proposed city Renewable Energy Zones around Sydney, Newcastle and Wollongong plus a far-west zone, while scaling back the New England zone.
campaignLedger.costing: No complete transition cost was stated in the cited report.
campaignLedger.geography: New England, far-west NSW, Sydney, Newcastle and Wollongong.
campaignLedger.verification: Test transmission contracts, sunk costs, generation capacity, reliability modelling, landholder effects and delivery timelines.

campaignLedger.title: Coal, nuclear and uranium policy shift
campaignLedger.summary: New NSW leader Mike Newman argued for continued coal generation, nuclear investment, reversing uranium-mining restrictions and abandoning Renewable Energy Zones.
campaignLedger.costing: No full fiscal, regulatory or project timetable was reported with the announcement.
campaignLedger.geography: Newman plans to contest Cessnock; the energy proposals have statewide and regional impacts.
campaignLedger.verification: Check state and federal legal powers, plant lead times, grid modelling, waste arrangements, private investment assumptions and affected communities.

campaignLedger.title: Regional payroll tax removal and metropolitan rate cut
campaignLedger.summary: One Nation proposed removing payroll tax in regional NSW and halving it in metropolitan areas.
campaignLedger.costing: No comprehensive cost or boundary definition was reported with the announcement.
campaignLedger.geography: Depends critically on how regional and metropolitan employers and payrolls are defined.
campaignLedger.verification: Request the revenue cost, anti-avoidance rules, treatment of multi-location employers and the exact geographic classification.

interstateLens.title: Queensland 2024: change of government with a regional path
interstateLens.facts: The LNP won 52 of 93 seats, Labor 36, Katter's Australian Party 3, the Greens 1 and an independent 1.
interstateLens.nswLens: The result shows how geographically concentrated issue salience can produce a change of government. For NSW, test regional and outer-suburban issue maps rather than assuming one statewide swing.
interstateLens.caveat: Queensland uses compulsory preferential voting, unlike NSW Assembly optional preferential voting.

interstateLens.title: Western Australia 2025: a government can win comfortably while losing altitude
interstateLens.facts: WA Labor won a third term despite a large swing away from its 2021 landslide. In the upper house it fell to 16 of 37 seats and lost sole control.
interstateLens.nswLens: Separate the binary question of who wins from mandate, swing, chamber control and the rebuilding capacity of an opposition.
interstateLens.caveat: WA changed its Legislative Council system before this election; institutional comparisons require care.

interstateLens.title: Tasmania 2025: fragmented chambers and negotiation
interstateLens.facts: The final 35-member lower house comprised 14 Liberals, 10 Labor, 5 Greens, 1 Shooters, Fishers and Farmers member and 5 independents.
interstateLens.nswLens: Minority arithmetic is not merely a seat total: confidence, supply, issue-by-issue support and relationships with individual crossbenchers matter.
interstateLens.caveat: Tasmania uses multi-member Hare–Clark electorates, so candidate and party dynamics are not directly transferable to NSW.

interstateLens.title: South Australia 2026: major-party disruption on the right
interstateLens.facts: Labor won 34 of 47 lower-house seats, Liberal 5, One Nation 4 and others 4. One Nation recorded 22.9% of the primary vote statewide.
interstateLens.nswLens: Watch whether a rising minor-party primary vote changes final pairings, preference exhaustion and Coalition resource choices in NSW — particularly outside inner Sydney.
interstateLens.caveat: Do not transplant SA vote shares into NSW; parties, electoral systems, candidates and local political conditions differ.

newsroomScenarios.prompt: A colleague says a statewide 4-point swing means every seat below 4% will change hands. What is your correction?
newsroomScenarios.answer: A uniform swing is a benchmark, not a forecast. Check regional variation, the actual final pairing, optional-preference exhaustion, incumbency, candidates, local issues and uncertainty before naming likely gains.

newsroomScenarios.prompt: A party announces a $3 billion transport plan at a marginal-seat event. What goes into the first filing note?
newsroomScenarios.answer: Record the exact commitment, years covered, capital/recurrent split, funding source, new-versus-recycled money, delivery milestones, dependencies, affected electorates, source document and unanswered questions.

newsroomScenarios.prompt: A campaign gives you an internal poll showing its candidate ahead by two points. What must you establish before reporting it?
newsroomScenarios.answer: Commissioner, pollster, sample, field dates, method, question order and wording, undecided treatment, full primary figures, preference assumptions, whether other results were withheld and why it was released now.

newsroomScenarios.prompt: The indicative election-night TCP is Labor–Liberal, but an independent is running second on primaries. What is the danger?
newsroomScenarios.answer: The selected indicative pair may be wrong. A later three-candidate-preferred or full distribution can produce a different final pair, so the displayed TCP swing may not describe the real contest.

newsroomScenarios.prompt: One early booth shows a 12-point swing. What do you compare before treating it as a seat trend?
newsroomScenarios.answer: Match the booth and boundaries, compare vote type and count completeness, inspect turnout and candidate field, then look for similar movement across demographically and geographically comparable booths.

newsroomScenarios.prompt: A party labels a seat its number-one target. How do you test whether behaviour matches the claim?
newsroomScenarios.answer: Track repeated leader visits, candidate timing, staffing, volunteer shifts, paid and direct advertising, local policy work, fundraising and whether the opponent diverts resources defensively.

newsroomScenarios.prompt: Residents blame the state MP for a council development approval and a federal migration setting. What is the reporting move?
newsroomScenarios.answer: Map each decision to the responsible level of government, then report any genuine state levers or political advocacy without collapsing distinct jurisdictions and boundaries.

newsroomScenarios.prompt: A seat's official 2023 winner differs from its current member's party. Which baseline belongs in copy?
newsroomScenarios.answer: State both with dates: the official 2023 result for historical comparison and the current holder/current analyst margin for today's political position, explaining the event that changed it.
checklist: Keep official and analyst figures distinct
